peer_results.rationale: No candidate was sufficiently comparable. BAC's candidate bac_2024_8_D044 discusses the estimation of credit losses for charged-off loans (allowing expected cash flows up to unpaid principal balance), which is a general credit loss estimation policy, not specific to the accounting classification, measurement basis (lower of cost or market), or cash flow presentation of Loans Held-for-Sale (HFS) as detailed in Citi's disclosure. BAC's candidate bac_2024_8_D055 excludes LHFS from nonperforming loans but does not discuss HFS measurement or P&L recognition mechanics comparable to Citi's specific HFS policy.

comparisons.peer_summary: Loans include held for investment loans accounted for at amortized cost (net of allowance or fair value option) and held for sale loans at lower of cost or fair value. Interest is recognized on an accrual basis over the life of the loan.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs classify loans held for sale (HFS) and measure them at the lower of cost or fair/market value. Citi specifies 'lower of cost or market value' with gains/losses in Other revenue, while Goldman Sachs specifies 'lower of cost or fair value' and groups HFS loans within the broader Loans category alongside held-for-investment loans, noting they are not measured at amortized cost. Both disclosures confirm that HFS loans are accounted for differently from held-for-investment loans (which are at amortized cost or FV option).

sentences.text: With the exception of those loans for which the fair value option has been elected, HFS loans are accounted for at the lower of cost or market value, with any write-downs or subsequent recoveries charged to Other revenue.
Gains and losses on loans HFS are generally presented in Other revenue.

Loans includes (i) loans held for investment that are accounted for at amortized cost net of allowance for loan losses or at fair value under the fair value option and (ii) loans held for sale that are accounted for at the lower of cost or fair value.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit loss impact from loan sales
comparisons.peer_summary: Sales of loans may result in write-downs, recoveries, or changes in the allowance for credit losses recognized in the provision for credit losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose how gains, losses, write-downs, and recoveries related to loans held for sale (or loan sales generally) are recognized in the financial statements. Citi specifically states that gains/losses on HFS loans are presented in Other revenue, but gains on sales of charged-off loans are presented as gross credit recoveries in the Provision for credit losses. JPMorgan similarly notes that sales of loans (which include HFS loans) result in write-downs, recoveries, or changes in the allowance recognized in the provision for credit losses, aligning with Citi's treatment of charged-off loan recoveries in the provision.

sentences.text: With the exception of those loans for which the fair value option has been elected, HFS loans are accounted for at the lower of cost or market value, with any write-downs or subsequent recoveries charged to Other revenue.
Gains and losses on loans HFS are generally presented in Other revenue.
Gains on sales of fully or partially charged-off loans are presented as gross credit recoveries in the Provision for credit losses up to the amount of prior charge-offs.
In addition, the sale of loans may also result in write downs, recoveries or changes in the allowance recognized in the provision for credit losses.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit loss allowances for loans held for sale
comparisons.peer_summary: Allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies do not apply to loans and lending commitments held for sale because they are recognized at the lower of cost or fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Morgan Stanley both explicitly state that loans held for sale are recognized at the lower of cost (or fair value) and that specific accounting treatments for held-for-investment loans, such as the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies, do not apply to them. Citi notes write-downs are charged to Other revenue, while Morgan Stanley explicitly excludes these loans from credit loss allowances because they are carried at the lower of cost or fair value.
